prompt: What does Python's Global Interpreter Lock (GIL) primarily prevent?
choices: Two Python processes from running at the same time
More than one thread from executing Python bytecode at the exact same instant, within one process
Two variables from referencing the same object
Recursive functions from exceeding the call stack
explanation: The GIL is a per-process lock that lets only one thread run Python bytecode at a time, even on a multi-core machine - it's why CPU-bound Python threading rarely speeds things up (use multiprocessing for that instead), while I/O-bound threading still benefits since the GIL is released during I/O waits.
